description: Rentals returned exactly at either endpoint timestamp count toward the total.

a.request: Counting rentals per `customer_id` whose `return_date` falls from '2005-07-13 08:35:51' to '2005-08-09 05:58:16', with both endpoints included (comparing the timestamps as text), what is the sum of those per-customer counts, as a single row?
a.sql: SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total FROM (SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM rental WHERE CAST(return_date AS TEXT) >= '2005-07-13 08:35:51' AND CAST(return_date AS TEXT) <= '2005-08-09 05:58:16' GROUP BY customer_id) t

c.request: If I count each customer's (`customer_id`) rentals that were returned between '2005-07-13 08:35:51' and '2005-08-09 05:58:16' (comparing `return_date` as text), what do those per-customer counts add up to? Give it as a single row. Rentals returned exactly at either endpoint timestamp count toward the total.

d.request: Sum, across customers, of each customer's count of rentals whose `return_date` (compared as text) is between '2005-07-13 08:35:51' and '2005-08-09 05:58:16' inclusive of both endpoint timestamps, returned as a single row with one total.
d.sql: SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total FROM (SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM rental WHERE CAST(return_date AS TEXT) BETWEEN '2005-07-13 08:35:51' AND '2005-08-09 05:58:16' GROUP BY customer_id) AS t

b.request: Total number of rentals across all customers whose `return_date`, compared as text, is between '2005-07-13 08:35:51' and '2005-08-09 05:58:16' inclusive of both endpoint timestamps (the sum of the per-customer rental counts), returned as a single row.
b.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_rentals FROM rental WHERE CAST(return_date AS TEXT) BETWEEN '2005-07-13 08:35:51' AND '2005-08-09 05:58:16'
b.raw: Total number of rentals across all customers whose `return_date`, compared as text, is between '2005-07-13 08:35:51' and '2005-08-09 05:58:16' inclusive of both endpoint timestamps (the sum of the per-customer rental counts), returned as a single row.
